message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Test

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    name: 'Test'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        name: Install pnpm
        id: pnpm-install
        with:
          version: 8.15.9
          run_install: false

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        name: Setup pnpm cache
        with:
          path: .pnpm-store/v3
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-test-${{ hashFiles('**/pnpm-lock.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-test-

      - name: Turbo Cache
        id: turbo-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: .turbo
          key: turbo-${{ github.job }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            turbo-${{ github.job }}-

      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build all packages
        run: pnpm build || pnpm build

      - name: Test
        run: pnpm run test

  prepare:
    name: Prepare packages
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          token: '${{ secrets.TOLGEE_MACHINE_PAT }}'

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        name: Install pnpm
        id: pnpm-install
        with:
          version: 8.15.9
          run_install: false

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        name: Setup pnpm cache
        with:
          path: |
            .pnpm-store/v3
            ~/.cache/Cypress
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-prepare-${{ hashFiles('**/pnpm-lock.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-prepare-

      - name: Turbo Cache
        id: turbo-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: .turbo
          key: turbo-prepare-${{ github.job }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            turbo-prepare-${{ github.job }}-

      - name: Create branch
        run: git checkout -b test.$(git ls-files -s packages | git hash-object --stdin)

      - name: Install root and packages dependencies
        run: |
          pnpm install --ignore-workspace
          pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile --filter='./packages/*'

      - name: test
        run: echo "test.$(git ls-files -s packages | git hash-object --stdin)"

      - name: Update version with lerna
        run: |
          pnpm exec lerna version prerelease --yes --conventional-prerelease --preid "test.$(git ls-files -s packages | git hash-object --stdin)" --ignore-scripts \
            --force-publish --no-push --no-git-tag-version --exact

      - name: Build packages
        run: pnpm build-packages

      - name: Set npm registry to GitHub Packages
        run: |
          echo "" >> .npmrc
          echo "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${{ secrets.TOLGEE_MACHINE_PAT }}" >> .npmrc
          echo "@tolgee:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com" >> .npmrc

      - name: Publish to GitHub Packages
        run: pnpm publish -r --no-git-checks --tag test
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{secrets.TOLGEE_MACHINE_PAT}}

      - id: set-dirs
        run: echo "dirs=$(ls | jq -R -s -c 'split("\n")[:-1] | map(select(. != "web-internal"))')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        working-directory: e2e/cypress/e2e

    outputs:
      dirs: ${{ steps.set-dirs.outputs.dirs }}

  cypress:
    name: E2e
    needs: prepare
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        app: ${{ fromJson(needs.prepare.outputs.dirs) }}
        node: [18, 20]
        exclude:
          - app: ngx
            # angular 20+ does not support node 18 anymore
            node: 18

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        name: Install pnpm
        id: pnpm-install
        with:
          version: 8.15.9
          run_install: false

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        name: Setup pnpm cache
        with:
          path: |
            .pnpm-store/v3
            ~/.cache/Cypress
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-cypress-${{ hashFiles('**/pnpm-lock.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-cypress-

      - name: Install for root and for e2e
        run: |
          pnpm install --ignore-workspace
          pnpm install --filter='./e2e'

      - name: Create branch
        run: git checkout -b test.$(git ls-files -s packages | git hash-object --stdin)

      - name: Update version with lerna
        run: |
          pnpm exec lerna version prerelease --yes --conventional-prerelease --preid "test.$(git ls-files -s packages | git hash-object --stdin)" --ignore-scripts \
            --force-publish --no-push --no-git-tag-version --exact

      - name: Remove 'workspace' field from package.json
        run: node scripts/packageJsonRemoveWorkspaces.js

      - name: Install testapp dependencies with npm
        run: |
          echo "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${{ secrets.TOLGEE_MACHINE_PAT }}" >> .npmrc
          echo "@tolgee:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com" >> .npmrc
          rm -rf node_modules
          npm install --force
        working-directory: testapps/${{matrix.app}}

      - name: Build testapp
        run: npm run build
        working-directory: testapps/${{matrix.app}}

      - name: Run e2e tests
        run: pnpm run e2e run --headed $(basename ${{matrix.app}}) --stdout prod,dev --skip-build

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: cypress
          path: |
            e2e/cypress/videos/**/*
            e2e/cypress/screenshots/**/*

  cypress-web-internal:
    name: E2e web-internal
    needs: prepare
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: [18, 20]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        name: Install pnpm
        id: pnpm-install
        with:
          version: 8.15.9
          run_install: false

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        name: Setup pnpm cache
        with:
          path: |
            .pnpm-store/v3
            ~/.cache/Cypress
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-cypress-${{ hashFiles('**/pnpm-lock.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-cypress-

      - name: Install for root and for e2e
        run: |
          pnpm install --ignore-workspace
          pnpm install --filter='./e2e'

      - name: Build web package
        run: |
          pnpm build --filter="@tolgee/web"

      - name: Run e2e tests
        run: pnpm run e2e run --headed web-internal --stdout prod,dev --skip-build

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: cypress
          path: |
            e2e/cypress/videos/**/*
            e2e/cypress/screenshots/**/*

  static-checks:
    name: Static check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        name: Install pnpm
        id: pnpm-install
        with:
          version: 8.15.9
          run_install: false

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        name: Setup pnpm cache
        with:
          path: .pnpm-store/v3
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-lint-${{ hashFiles('**/pnpm-lock.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-lint-

      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile

      - name: Eslint
        run: pnpm run eslint

      - name: Eslint
        run: pnpm --prefix e2e run eslint",
  "rationale": "Added custom job timeouts (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT) to all five jobs based on evidence showing 12.9% (free) / 8.1% (paid) VM time reduction and a measured experiment with 26.8% elapsed savings. The workflow previously had no timeouts, leaving jobs subject to the 6-hour default. Timeouts were set conservatively with operational headroom: test (10 min), prepare (15 min), cypress matrix jobs (30 min each), cypress-web-internal (30 min), static-checks (5 min), based on observed total run durations of 13-20 minutes in recent CI history. This preserves all build/test coverage and adds no new permissions or network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
message.reasoning:
Let me analyze the workflow and the evidence to determine if there's a suitable CI optimization to apply.

The workflow is a complex multi-job workflow for a TypeScript/JavaScript monorepo using pnpm, turbo, and Cypress for E2E testing. Let me look at the jobs:

1. `test` - Runs unit tests
2. `prepare` - Prepares packages for publishing
3. `cypress` - Runs E2E tests with matrix (multiple apps, node versions)
4. `cypress-web-internal` - Runs E2E tests for web-internal
5. `static-checks` - Runs eslint

Now let me look at the evidence patterns to see what optimizations might apply:

1. **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** - Add custom timeouts to jobs. The evidence shows this can save significant time (12.9% free, 8.1% paid). The workflow currently has no timeouts set.

2. **P-LIT-FAIL-FAST** - Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure. The cypress jobs use matrix strategy with `fail-fast: false`. This could be changed to `fail-fast: true` to save resources when a test fails.

3. **P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE** - Cancel superseded runs. This would require adding concurrency settings.

4. **P-LIT-GHA-CACHE** - Cache dependency downloads. The workflow already has caching for pnpm and turbo.

5. **P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE** - Share cached build dependencies. The workflow already uses actions/cache.

6. **P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER** - Filter workflow triggers by changed paths. Could add path filters to trigger only on relevant changes.

7. **P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW** - Skip explicitly dispensable workflow runs.

8. **P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE** - Pause repeatedly failing scheduled workflows. Not applicable as there are no scheduled workflows.

9. **P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE** - Suppress schedules during repository inactivity. Not applicable.

10. **P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST** - Run previously failing jobs first. Would require CI service changes.

11. **P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT** - Derive timeout candidates from successful history. Related to custom timeout.

12. **P-LIT-PRIORITIZE** - Prioritize tests for early failure feedback. Would require test configuration changes.

13. **P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY** - Prioritize queued builds. CI service level.

14. **P-LIT-SELECT** - Select tests using change dependencies. Would require test configuration changes.

15. **P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT** - Select builds using change or outcome predictions. CI service level.

16. **P-LIT-BAZEL-PARALLEL** - Tune Bazel build parallelism. Not applicable (not using Bazel).

17. **P-LIT-BAZEL-INCREMENTAL** - Cache Bazel build results. Not applicable.

18. **P-LIT-BAZEL-DEPS** - Evaluate dependency cache overhead. Not applicable.

19. **P-LIT-ENV-CACHE** - Reuse validated build environments. Not directly applicable.

20. **P-LIT-UNAFFECTED-STEPS** - Skip steps using traced dependencies. Would require CI service changes.

21. **P-LIT-SMELL-REPAIR** - Repair evidenced configuration smells. General guidance.

22. **P-LIT-DURATION-PREDICTION** - Predict duration to guide investigation. Research only.

23. **P-LIT-UNUSED-OUTPUTS** - Remove genuinely unused outputs. Could apply to artifacts.

24. **P-LIT-CONFIG-REUSE** - Reuse work across compatible configurations. Not directly applicable.

25. **P-LIT-UNUSED-DEP-SKIP** - Evaluate skipping unused-dependency updates. Not directly applicable.

Looking at the workflow, the most applicable optimizations seem to be:

1. **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** - Add timeouts to jobs to prevent runaway consumption. The workflow has no timeouts currently.

2. **P-LIT-FAIL-FAST** - The cypress and cypress-web-internal jobs use `fail-fast: false` in their matrix strategy. Changing to `fail-fast: true` would cancel remaining matrix jobs after a failure.

3. **P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE** - Add concurrency to cancel superseded runs on the same branch/PR.

Let me check the evidence for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT more carefully. The evidence shows:
- Experiment example with 26.8% elapsed savings
- Pattern shows 12.9% free, 8.1% paid VM time reduction
- Precondition: "Representative successful-duration history exists"
- Safety tests: "Cold dependency installation", "A deliberately hung step", "Slow valid run"

For P-LIT-FAIL-FAST:
- Evidence shows 2% free, 1.5% paid VM time reduction
- Precondition: "Matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable under an explicit study policy"
- Contraindications: "Every matrix outcome is required", "Full failure diagnostics are required"

For P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE:
- Evidence shows 1.9% free, 4.1% paid VM time reduction
- Precondition: "Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR", "A newer revision supersedes older checks"
- Contraindications: "Release or deployment work", "Distinct branches share a cancellation group"

The workflow has:
- Multiple jobs that could benefit from timeouts
- Matrix jobs with `fail-fast: false` that could be changed
- No concurrency settings for canceling stale runs

Let me think about which optimization is most supported and safe to apply.

The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT has the highest reported savings (12.9% free, 8.1% paid) and the experiment example shows 26.8% elapsed savings. However, we need to be careful about setting appropriate timeout values.

The P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is also applicable since the cypress jobs use matrix with `fail-fast: false`. However, the contraindication "Every matrix outcome is required" might apply if they need all matrix results for debugging.

The P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is also applicable and commonly used.

Looking at the experiment evidence for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (document_id: experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508), it shows a 26.8% elapsed savings with a 5-minute timeout added to a job that had median runtime of 34 seconds. That's a significant saving.

For the current workflow, I need to determine appropriate timeout values. Looking at the CI history:
- Recent successful runs take about 13-20 minutes total (from created_at to updated_at)
- The test job likely takes a few minutes
- The prepare job takes some time
- The cypress matrix jobs run in parallel

Since we don't have per-job timing data, I should be conservative with timeouts. A common practice is to set timeouts to 2-3x the expected runtime.

However, the instruction says to use retrieved evidence and repository files to check prerequisites. The evidence for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT requires "Representative successful-duration history exists". We have some CI history but not per-job breakdown.

Let me also consider P-LIT-FAIL-FAST. The cypress job has:
```yaml

  fail-fast: false
  matrix:
    app: ${{ fromJson(needs.prepare.outputs.dirs) }}
    node: [18, 20]

```

And cypress-web-internal has:

Changing `fail-fast: false` to `fail-fast: true` would cancel remaining matrix jobs when one fails. This is a simple change with evidence support.

But the contraindication "Every matrix outcome is required" - for E2E tests, they might want to see all failures across different apps/node versions. However, the pattern evidence suggests this saves resources.

Let me also consider P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE. Adding concurrency at the workflow level:
```yaml

  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

This would cancel previous runs on the same branch when a new push occurs. This is a very common optimization.

Now, which one to choose? The instruction says "Propose any evidence-supported CI optimization that fits this workflow" and "Choose APPLY for a supported change and include the complete updated workflow in workflow_yaml."

I think the most impactful and safe change would be adding **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** to jobs, as it has the highest reported savings. But I need to set reasonable timeout values.

Alternatively, **P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE** (concurrency) is very safe and commonly used.

Or **P-LIT-FAIL-FAST** for the matrix jobs.

Let me check if there are any experiment examples that closely match this workflow. The experiment for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT was on a Node.js project with eslint, typecheck, etc. - somewhat similar.

The experiment for P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE shows adding pip cache to a Python project - not directly applicable since this workflow already has pnpm cache.

Given the evidence, I think **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** has the strongest evidence (26.8% savings in experiment, 12.9%/8.1% in paper). However, setting appropriate timeouts requires knowledge of job durations.

Looking at the workflow jobs:
- `test`: runs pnpm install, build, test - probably 3-5 minutes
- `prepare`: more complex, publishes packages - probably 5-10 minutes
- `cypress`: E2E tests - could be 10-20 minutes per matrix job
- `cypress-web-internal`: similar

Since we don't have exact per-job timing, I could add conservative timeouts. But the pattern says "Choose an explicit budget with operational headroom" and "Measure false timeout failures separately".

Alternatively, **P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE** is safer because it doesn't risk timing out valid runs. The evidence shows 1.9% free, 4.1% paid reduction.

But wait, the workflow has multiple jobs that might need to run independently. The concurrency would cancel the entire workflow run when a new one starts on the same ref. That's usually desired for PRs and branches.

Actually, looking at the workflow triggers:
```yaml

  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
```

For pull_request, each PR gets its own ref (refs/pull/X/merge), so concurrency would cancel previous runs on the same PR. For push to main, it would cancel previous main runs. This is generally safe.

Let me also consider that the prepare job uses a secret token (TOLGEE_MACHINE_PAT) and publishes to GitHub Packages. Canceling a publish job mid-way could leave things in a bad state. But the concurrency cancel-in-progress only cancels at job boundaries, not mid-job. And the prepare job has `needs: []` (no needs), while cypress jobs need prepare. So if a new run starts, it would cancel the old prepare job if it's still running, or the cypress jobs if they're queued.

Actually, `cancel-in-progress: true` cancels in-progress runs, meaning it can cancel a running job. This could be problematic for the prepare job which publishes packages. The contraindication for P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE includes "Release or deployment work".

So maybe concurrency is not ideal for this workflow due to the publish step.

What about P-LIT-FAIL-FAST for the matrix jobs? The cypress and cypress-web-internal jobs are E2E tests. If one matrix combination fails, do they need the others to run? The contraindication "Every matrix outcome is required" and "Full failure diagnostics are required" might apply. But the pattern evidence suggests it saves resources.

What about P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT? This adds timeouts to individual jobs. This is safer than concurrency because it doesn't cancel jobs due to new pushes, only due to hanging. The experiment shows significant savings.

Given the CI history shows runs taking 13-20 minutes total, and the workflow has 5 jobs (some parallel), I could add reasonable timeouts:
- test: 10 minutes
- prepare: 15 minutes  
- cypress: 30 minutes (matrix jobs run in parallel, each might take 10-20 min)
- cypress-web-internal: 30 minutes
- static-checks: 5 minutes

But I need to be careful not to set timeouts too low. The pattern says "Choose an explicit budget with operational headroom".

Actually, looking at the experiment example for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, they added `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job with median runtime of 34 seconds. That's ~9x headroom. For a job taking 5 minutes, 10 minutes would be 2x headroom.

Let me check the GitHub Actions default timeout - it's 6 hours (360 minutes) for jobs. So any reasonable timeout we set will be much lower.

I think the most evidence-supported and safe optimization is **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** based on the experiment showing 26.8% savings and the pattern reporting 12.9%/8.1% reduction. The workflow currently has no timeouts at all.

However, I need to set appropriate values. Since I don't have per-job timing data, I'll use conservative estimates based on the total run times (13-20 minutes) and job complexity.

Let me also consider that the evidence_ids must be from the provided evidence. The experiment evidence for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is document_id: "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508" and the pattern is "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT".

I'll go with adding custom timeouts to all jobs. This is a minimal change that preserves all functionality and has strong evidence support.

Let me construct the updated workflow with timeout-minutes added to each job.

For the test job: runs pnpm install, build, test. Probably 3-5 min. Set to 10 min.
For prepare job: more complex, publishes packages. Probably 5-10 min. Set to 15 min.
For cypress job: matrix of E2E tests. Each matrix job might take 10-20 min. Set to 30 min.
For cypress-web-internal: similar. Set to 30 min.
